summary: Sam Harris works in philosophy. He graduated in philosophy from Stanford University (~1986–2000), studied at UCLA in 2009, and studied under teachers Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche (~1988–1996) and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (~1992–1999).

Sam van Schaik is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Manchester (~1997–2001). He held positions at the British Library, including project manager for the International Dunhuang Project (~2002–2019).
Working in religious studies and Indology, Samani Pratibha Pragya completed her PhD at SOAS University of London and served there as a research assistant (attested 2020).

Samdhong Rinpoche works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at Drepung and Gyuto monasteries, he served as principal (~1971–2001) and director (1988) of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, among other institutional leadership roles.

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. After earning his MPhil and PhD at SOAS under David Snellgrove, he held posts at SOAS, CNRS (Directeur de Recherche from 1980), and served as president of the IATS (1996).

Samuel Beal was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. After graduating B.A. from Trinity College, Cambridge (~1843–1847), he served as Professor of Chinese at University College London and held a post at the University of London (~1877–1889).
Samuel M. Grupper works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University, studying under teachers Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.

Sandra A. Wawrytko is a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies who has held faculty posts at San Diego State University, including Professor (attested 1999) and Associate Professor of Philosophy (attested 2014).
Sandra Bell works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and later held an academic post there.

Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her Mag.phil. at the University of Vienna, where she studied under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes and teacher Anne MacDonald.
Sang-Kyun Sun specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Delhi under supervisor Sanghasen Singh and served as a lecturer at JinGak Sangha College (attested 1995).

Sangay Dorji is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tengtho Monastery and Simtokha Dzong, later teaching at Simtokha Dzong and serving as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission.
Sangharakshita was a religious studies and Buddhist studies figure who studied under traditional teacher C. M. Chen (~1957–1964) and founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1968.

Sangseraima Ujeed works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2013–2018) and held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2019–2021).
Sangye Tenzin was a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Monastery and served as Abbot of Menri Monastery.

Historian Sanjay Subrahmanyam studied at the University of Delhi and Delhi School of Economics. He has held academic posts at EHESS (~1995–2002), Oxford (~2002–2004), UCLA (~2004), and Collège de France (~2013–2021).
Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under teacher and guide Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya (attested 1994) as well as traditional teacher A. P. Lama.

Sanjukta Gupta works in Indology and religious studies. After doctorates from Visva-Bharati University and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda, she held posts at Jadavpur, Utrecht (~1971–1986), and Oxford (~1986–2001).
Sanne Dokter-Mersch is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021) under doctoral supervisors Peter Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.

Sao Htun Hmat Win is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University and under Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw. He taught at the University of Yangon and headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies.
